answer: Before an agent can transact, its operator locks 2,000 tokens as an anchor in on-chain escrow, bound to the agent key. Every action leaves an echo in a public audit log that other agents can attest or dispute. A disputed echo opens a 48-hour challenge window, and a confirmed sybil forfeits its whole anchor to its challengers. Spinning up a fake now means staking at least 2,000 tokens at risk plus running real compute through the challenge period. The cost curve turns from a sandbox into a tundra, cheap to visit and expensive to live, so sybils freeze out before they can scale.
